In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({e}^{x})^{′}\cdot cos⁡x-{e}^{x}\cdot (cos⁡x)^{′}}{(cos⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}cos⁡x+{e}^{x}sin⁡x}{(cos⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x)}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
